A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LAGEA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original Meta-World MT10 and Fetch experiments, learning curves, component ablations, encoder comparisons and wall-clock measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds keyframe-sampling comparisons and evaluations under unseen camera viewpoints.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix G retain the same structured feedback generation, keyframe weighting, alignment losses, delta rewards and adaptive SAC reward shaping. The new experiments evaluate the existing method.

E1.justification: Meta-World MT10 and Fetch task coverage is retained. Section 4.3.5 adds three unseen camera viewpoints on five existing observable MT10 tasks, extending evaluation to new visual input conditions.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds Random KF and Uniform KF as evaluated sampling controls. These differ from v2's ablation using uniform per-step weights. The existing RL baselines and VLM/text-encoder comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 introduces training at one camera viewpoint followed by zero-shot evaluation at three held-out viewpoints, plus a comparison varying keyframe-sampling strategy. These are protocols for added experiments; previously reported benchmark settings, metrics and implementation configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially extends robustness analysis through direct random/uniform keyframe-selection controls across five tasks and a new held-out-camera study. These test selector specificity and visual distribution shift beyond v2's retained component-removal, feedback-quality and encoder analyses.

E5.justification: Existing seed counts and mean/standard-deviation reporting are retained. However, new Tables 4 and 6 specify three seeds while their LAGEA reference entries match five-seed Table 2, including 96 (8) for button press; Appendix C's three-seed counterpart remains 93.33 (9.43). Whether reference statistics were recomputed, reused or mislabeled is unresolved.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and appendix results remain unchanged. New Table 4 reports average success of 68%, 67.33% and 80% for Random KF, Uniform KF and LAGEA. New Table 6 reports held-out-view averages of 79.33%, 77.33% and 79.33%. These are added comparisons and conditions, not demonstrated performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: The saliency definitions, alignment objectives, reward potentials and adaptive-schedule equations are mathematically unchanged. Edits to equation punctuation and spacing introduce no new definitions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the central claims about temporally grounded language feedback, improved success and faster convergence. The new experiments support existing claims rather than redefine the main contributions.

C2.justification: Section 4.3.5 newly interprets the camera experiments as evidence of viewpoint robustness while explicitly excluding severe self-occlusion and cluttered-scene occlusion. The earlier hallucination, real-robot and long-horizon limitations are retained verbatim, moving from Appendix M into the conclusion.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-code repository link in the abstract, absent from v2. Hardware, software versions, environment specifications and algorithm documentation remain unchanged. The PDFs establish the new access pointer, not the repository's contents or availability.

R1.justification: The M3-Embedding reference receives corrected authorship and publication metadata, and duplicate Lynch-Sermanet entries sharing the same arXiv identifier are consolidated. These changes do not add distinct cited research or alter the paper's positioning.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized revisions around the expanded experiments, adds Section 4.3.5, moves the limitations paragraph into the conclusion, changes author order and publication/header text, and corrects bibliography entries. Most prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 4 and 6 and adjusts table numbering and surrounding page layout. The structured-feedback table becomes Table 5, and appendix tables are renumbered. Existing figures, plots and their underlying visual content are retained.

improvement.justification: The added sampling controls and held-out-viewpoint tests address questions left experimentally untested in v2. The explicit occlusion boundary, more visible existing limitations and code-access pointer also improve assessment of the work. These are limited gains: the core results are unchanged, and the unexplained seed-count attribution in the new tables weakens confidence in their exact comparisons.
